text: You have 180 days from the date of your accident to tell us about a claim. You can file it in the member portal, in the Harbor Mutual app, or by calling member services, and you'll need the date of the accident, a short description of what happened, and the bills or a statement from the doctor who treated you. Claims sent after 180 days may still be reviewed, but payment isn't guaranteed, so it's best to file as soon as you can, and you can send any documents you don't have yet later.

Prescription drugs and medications aren't covered by this plan, even when they're prescribed for an injury from a covered accident. They're usually covered by your major medical plan, so give the pharmacy that plan's card. The visits, treatment and services this plan does cover are still paid as scheduled.

Yes, injuries from amateur sports and recreation are covered, including skiing, snowboarding, cycling, running, swimming, hiking and golf, whether it's school teams, club and league play, pickup games or fitness classes. The exception is playing professionally, meaning you're paid to play or compete — coaching or refereeing for pay doesn't count as playing professionally, so an injury while doing either is covered.

If you lose your member ID card, you can order a new one in the member portal or the Harbor Mutual app, or by calling member services. A new card arrives by mail in 7 to 10 days, and the app shows a digital card you can use right away.

If you miss a premium payment, you have a 31-day grace period to pay before your coverage ends, and we'll send you a reminder by email. Accidents that happen during the grace period are covered once the premium is paid.
You can change your address in the member portal or the app under Profile, or by calling member services.

Yes, member services is open Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Eastern time.

Yes, you can add your new baby within 31 days of the birth, or during open enrollment from November 1 to December 15. If your plan is through your employer, make the change through your employer's benefits office, and it takes effect on the first day of the month after we receive it.

No, we never sell your information. We use it only to run your plan and pay your claims, and you can ask for a copy of the records we keep about you or ask us to correct something that's wrong through the member portal.
